_comment: Tracks social post topics already drafted, so the influencer agent doesn't repeat itself. Each entry: { date, slug, topic }. The agent reads this before picking a new topic — avoid anything covered in the last 14 days.

entries.topic: ambient transcription reduces the paperwork tax
a vague Plan section is the same as no plan at all
a free tool that turns rough session notes into a structured SOAP or EMDR note, no signup
not every no-show has the same cause - separating logistics failures (double-booking, a missing Meet link) from genuine forgetting or ambivalence
recording consent and AI-processing consent are legally and practically distinct - most intake flows still treat them as one checkbox
the online notetaker bot joins a Google Meet call like a silent observer - no camera, no chat, just audio - and feeds the same note pipeline as in-person sessions
"encrypted" in a privacy policy usually just means the connection - field-level encryption at rest and per-therapist row-level security are a different claim
switching practice management tools usually means retyping every existing patient by hand - Kith imports patients straight from a CSV or Excel export instead
the biggest confidentiality risk in an online session usually isn't the video platform - it's who else is actually in the room
recurring appointments in Kith generate a fresh Google Meet link for every occurrence automatically - not one reused link that gets copied, lost, or goes stale over weeks of sessions
Kith now generates DAP and BIRP notes, not just SOAP and EMDR - BIRP's Intervention field is real added structure for insurance/agency documentation requirements

when Kith drafts a new note, it pulls the last 4 sessions - summary, homework, next-session plan, risk level - to track trajectory across sessions and flag anything planned earlier that never got followed up on
a session note is supposed to outlive whatever software it was written in - PDF export as a practical ownership question, not a feature checkbox
the free SOAP note template guide - the hard part was never the blank format, it's deciding what actually belongs in each section

AI note-drafting is usually priced as an upsell on top of a base EHR subscription - Kith builds the ambient transcription + note pipeline into the free plan instead of gating it behind a per-clinician add-on fee

one AI call asked to both compress a raw session transcript and structure it into a SOAP note tends to do both jobs badly - Kith runs a two-layer pipeline instead, one pass to compress and a separate pass to structure
note-writing speed varies less by template quality than by how soon after the session the note gets written - immediacy beats formatting, and that's the gap ambient transcription closes by default

most scheduling tools trust the therapist not to double-book - Kith actually checks for overlapping appointments before confirming a booking, and fails closed rather than silently confirming if the check itself breaks
most EHR trials ask for a credit card before you've even tried the product - Kith's free plan skips that entirely, no card required to start
UK GDPR: your notetaking software is a data processor, you're the controller - the compliance obligation is yours first, not something a vendor's privacy page covers for you

India's DPDP Act 2023 dropped the special "sensitive personal data" tier that earlier drafts had for health information - therapy notes get the same baseline protection as everything else, not an extra checklist

most scheduling software markets automated SMS/email reminders sent to the patient as the no-show fix - Kith doesn't send those today, and it's more useful to say so directly than let the feature list imply it

Kith's Google Calendar sync pulls your existing calendar events in to check for conflicts before booking - it doesn't push Kith appointments back out to Google Calendar yet. Worth saying plainly rather than letting "calendar sync" imply both directions.

most AI scribes still require you to manually hit record - a browser extension, app, or button - at the start of a session. Kith's in-person capture is ambient through the device mic instead, nothing to remember to press.

the homework or next-session plan a therapist assigns at the end of a session usually lives in a sticky note or memory, not the chart - Kith's note pipeline writes it into its own structured field on every note instead

a SOAP note and a plain-English session summary answer different questions - the note is for the chart/audit trail, the summary is for quickly recalling what actually happened without re-reading clinical language. Kith's note pipeline generates both, plus a separate key-points list, from the same session automatically.

most EHR breaches don't expose one therapist's caseload - they expose everyone's, because isolation between accounts is enforced at the app layer instead of the database layer. Kith enforces row-level security at the database layer, so one compromised login can't read another therapist's patient data.

solo therapists commonly patch together five disconnected subscriptions (EHR, scheduling, video, intake) that don't share data - Kith keeps scheduling, patient records, and session notes in one free plan instead

recording consent and AI-processing consent are legally and practically distinct - most intake flows still bundle both into one signature, and it's the specific gap AI vendor privacy policies keep getting called out for

most AI notetakers for therapy still require you to manually start a recording (button, extension, browser tab) - Kith's in-person capture is ambient through the device mic instead, nothing to press, riffing on the published Kith vs Upheal comparison post

a Google Calendar invite titled with a client's name is itself a small data leak, separate from the video platform - if the calendar is shared with a receptionist or practice partner, event visibility needs to be private, not just the meeting link (backfilled - drafted 2026-08-26 but not committed until this run)

Kith's 15-minute pre-session heads-up notifies the therapist, not the patient - worth being precise about who a 'reminder' feature is actually for, since most scheduling software marketing means the opposite

a note pulled from a fixed template still starts from a blank box for every client, which is where generic, recycled-sounding language comes from - Kith's notes are built from what was actually said in the session, not filled into a template afterward

Kith's session capture is fully automatic within its scope but has no override outside it - mic for in-person, a notetaker bot for Google Meet online - no upload option, no dictate-a-recap fallback, so a session not captured live through one of those two paths has no note generated

Kith's AI note pipeline produces a draft after the session - nothing writes into the patient's chart automatically, the therapist reads and edits it first - a first pass, not a finished unreviewed entry

SimplePractice's AI note-taking isn't included in any base tier - it's a $17.50-29.50/mo per-clinician add-on stacked on top of $49-99/mo base pricing, which comes to $210-354/year just for AI notes. Kith bundles ambient transcription + AI notes into the free plan instead, riffing on the published Kith vs SimplePractice comparison post

Mentalyc prices AI notes on a tiered monthly-note-allowance model - 40 notes for $19.99/mo up to 330 for $119.99/mo - so seeing more clients costs more every month just for notes. Kith's AI note pipeline is unlimited on the free plan, riffing on the published Kith vs Mentalyc comparison post

insurance and Medicaid documentation usually wants DAP or BIRP, not SOAP - most AI note tools only speak one format. Kith drafts SOAP, DAP, BIRP, or EMDR from the same session, so note format doesn't dictate which tool a therapist can use
